content: {"rule":"K-S2","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text assigns UNDERDETERMINED and reasons from Luke 2:48-49's two father-references, which is the dual-sense/open-verse situation the rule governs.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"UNDERDETERMINED -- answered in [CR2] §5 and [CR3] LINK 4; Mary's phrase \"thy father\" is immediately qualified by the child's reference to \"my Father's business.\"","rule_words":"That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.","room":"\"A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.\" I weighed (1) treating both father-references as standing together versus (2) treating the second as making the verse open/underdetermined; the judge chose the latter.","why":"By calling the verse UNDERDETERMINED because \"thy father\" is qualified by \"my Father's business,\" the judge treats the two-sense verse as open, which K-S2 forbids."}
